paper.title: On Thompson Sampling with Langevin Algorithms

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed stochastic bandit with log-concave parametric reward families (exact Thompson sampling)
unmapped: rewards of arm a follow a known parametric family p_a(x|theta_a), theta_a in R^{d_a}, log-likelihood m_a-strongly concave and L_a-smooth in theta around theta_a^* (Assumption 1-Local)
true reward distribution nu_a-strongly log-concave in x with grad_theta log p L_a-Lipschitz in x (Assumption 2); rewards unbounded
mean reward linear in parameter: E[X]=alpha_a^T theta_a with known alpha_a, ||alpha_a||=A_a
learner knows the problem constants d_a, m_a, L_a, nu_a used to set the posterior scaling gamma_a
settings.definition_quote: we assume that the reward distribution for each arm is a member of a parametric family parametrized by $\theta_a \in \mb{R}^{d_a}$ such that the true reward distribution is $p_a(X)=p_a(X ;\theta_a^*)$, where $\theta_a^*$ is unknown. Moreover, we assume throughout this paper that the parametric families are log-concave and Lipschitz smooth in $\theta_a$

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed stochastic bandit with log-concave parametric reward families (approximate Thompson sampling, Assumptions 1-Uniform to 4)
unmapped: log-likelihood uniformly m_a-strongly concave and L_a-smooth in theta for all theta (Assumption 1-Uniform)
joint Lipschitz smoothness of grad_theta log p_a(x|theta) in (theta, x) (Assumption 4, for SGLD)
true reward distribution nu_a-strongly log-concave in x (Assumption 2); rewards unbounded
mean reward linear in parameter: E[X]=alpha_a^T theta_a, ||alpha_a||=A_a
learner knows d_a, m_a, L_a, nu_a used to set step size, number of steps, batch size and gamma_a
settings.definition_quote: Assume that $\log p_a(x|\theta_a)$ is $L_a$-smooth and $m_a$-strongly concave over the parameter $\theta_a$ ... Assume a joint Lipschitz smoothness condition, which strengthens Assumptions 1-Uniform and 2 to impose the Lipschitz smoothness on the entire bivariate function $\log p_a(x;\theta)$

algorithms.name: Thompson sampling with exact scaled posterior
Thompson sampling with ULA (unadjusted Langevin algorithm, warm-started)
Thompson sampling with SGLD (stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics, warm-started)

bound.expression_latex: \sum_{a>1} \frac{ C A_a^2}{m_a\Delta_a}\left(\log B_a+d_a^2\kappa_a^3+d_a\kappa_a^3 \log(T)\right)+\sqrt{\kappa_1 B_1}\frac{C A_1^2}{m_1\Delta_a} \left(1+\log B_1+d_1^2\kappa_1^3\right) +\Delta_a

symbols.C_univ: universal constant independent of problem parameters
symbols.A_a: norm of the vector alpha_a mapping parameter to mean reward of arm a
symbols.m_a: strong log-concavity parameter of the likelihood in theta for arm a
symbols.kappa_a: condition number max(L_a/m_a, L_a/nu_a) of arm a
symbols.B_a: prior quality max_theta pi_a(theta)/pi_a(theta_a^*) for arm a

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 (log-concave smooth likelihood around theta*, strongly log-concave true reward distribution, log-concave smooth prior)
mean reward is linear alpha_a^T theta_a
tuning: gamma_a = 1/(8 d_a kappa_a^3) (appendix: nu_a m_a^2/(8 d_a L_a^3))

source.label: thm:exact_regret
source.quote: When the likelihood and true reward distributions satisfy Assumptions 1-3 and $\gamma_a=\frac{1}{8d_a \kappa_a^3}$ we have that the expected regret after $T>0$ rounds of Thompson sampling with exact sampling satisfies: \mb{E}[R(T)]\le \sum_{a>1} \frac{ C A_a^2}{m_a\Delta_a}\left(\log B_a+d_a^2\kappa_a^3+d_a\kappa_a^3 \log(T)\right)+\sqrt{\kappa_1 B_1}\frac{C A_1^2}{m_1\Delta_a} \left(1+\log B_1+d_1^2\kappa_1^3\right) +\Delta_a

results.notes: Statement places the optimal-arm term and trailing Delta_a outside the sum with an unbound Delta_a; the proof bounds per-arm E[T_a], so I placed all terms inside sum_subopt. Appendix proof has Delta_a^2 in the optimal-arm term. Regret defined via means, so pseudo-regret. Algorithm does not use T.

bound.expression: sum_subopt(C_univ*A_a**2/(m_a*Delta_i)*(log(B_a) + d_a + d_a**2*kappa_a**2*log(T)) + sqrt(B_1)*C_univ*A_1**2/(m_1*Delta_i)*(1 + log(B_1) + d_1**2*kappa_1**2 + d_1*kappa_1**2*log(T)) + 3*Delta_i)
bound.expression_latex: \sum_{a>1} \frac{C A_a^2}{ m_a\Delta_a}\left( \log B_a+d_a+ d_a^2\kappa_a^2 \log T \right)+\sqrt{B_1}\frac{C  A_1^2}{m_1\Delta_a}\left( 1+\log B_1+d_1^2\kappa_1^2 +d_1\kappa_1^2\log{T}\right) +3\Delta_a

symbols.C_univ: universal constant independent of problem parameters
symbols.m_a: strong log-concavity parameter of the likelihood in theta

conditions: mean reward is linear alpha_a^T theta_a
tuning: step size h^(n) = m_a/(32 n (L_a + L_a/n)^2) = O(1/(n L_a kappa_a))
number of steps N = 640 (L_a+L_a/n)^2/m_a^2 = O(kappa_a^2), warm-started from previous sample
gamma_a = nu_a m_a^2/(32(16 L_a nu_a m_a + 4 d_a L_a^3)) = O(1/(d_a kappa_a^3))
output perturbed by N(0, 1/(n L_a gamma_a) I)

source.label: thm:approx_regret
source.quote: When the likelihood and true reward distributions satisfy Assumptions 1-4: we have that the expected regret after $T>0$ rounds of Thompson sampling with the (stochastic gradient) ULA method with the hyper-parameters and runtime as described in Theorem~\ref{theorem3} satisfies: \mb{E}[R(T)]\le \sum_{a>1} \frac{C A_a^2}{ m_a\Delta_a}\left( \log B_a+d_a+ d_a^2\kappa_a^2 \log T \right)+\sqrt{B_1}\frac{C  A_1^2}{m_1\Delta_a}\left( 1+\log B_1+d_1^2\kappa_1^2 +d_1\kappa_1^2\log{T}\right) +3\Delta_a.

results.notes: ULA instance of Theorem 4. Per-iteration cost grows with n (full gradient) but number of iterations constant. Terms outside the sum in the statement were placed inside sum_subopt (per-arm proof). Appendix restatement (Theorem E.2) uses kappa_a = L_a/m_a.
